key_insight: PPy-PVA hydrogel geometry tunes drug transport by altering microstructure and local electric fields, offering an alternative to current-density modulation.
engineering_relevance: Geometry-based hydrogel design could enable adjustable iontophoretic delivery without independently tuning current density for each design.
method: Fabricated BSA-loaded PPy-PVA hydrogels in five geometries, including Hilbert curve-based designs.
Evaluated electric fields using finite element analysis and microstructure using scanning electron microscopy.
Measured passive and iontophoretic transport in Franz diffusion cells with artificial membranes.
evidence_signal: The five geometries produced distinct transport profiles, while iontophoresis enhanced permeability over passive diffusion, with average iontophoretic permeability reported as (3.80 ± 1.93) × 10^-5.
watch_item: Artificial-membrane testing does not establish performance in human skin, and the abstract reports FEM analysis rather than an AI surrogate.
paper_title: Geometry-Dependent Properties of Physically Crosslinked PPy-PVA Hydrogels Enable Tunable Iontophoretic Drug Delivery
